findings.title: Associates is compiled into the Genesis candidate instead of isolated as a future DLC
evidence: policy.rs maps role 2 to CCC_ASSOCIATE_RATE_BPS
set_eligibility accepts every role for which role_rate returns Some
open_position has no Associates feature-state check
The public economic policy fixes cccAssociate at 2000 bps
impact: After common V2 activation, the administrator can enable an Associate immediately
Public claims that Associates is not part of Genesis are not enforced by code
A separate audit or activation transaction is not mandatory
remediation: Remove role 2 from the Genesis binary, or add an immutable default-off DLC state with separate authority and policy hash
Require a separately reviewed one-way activation instruction
Prove Genesis instructions cannot create or use Associate eligibility

findings.title: No T+1-week Associates activation bound exists
evidence: set_eligibility checks config.active but not Genesis time
open_position checks config.active but not feature time
CCC round zero opens at Genesis plus 24 hours, which is a different clock and does not gate Associate eligibility
impact: Associate access can begin immediately after V2 activation
No latest, exact, or earliest one-week policy can be audited
Operators can conflate the 24-hour CCC round delay with DLC activation
remediation: Specify one exact T+1-week semantic
Store canonical Genesis and DLC activation state
Add T-1, T, T+1 boundary tests and irreversible terminal behavior

findings.title: Wallet/X/Premium qualification is absent from Associate eligibility
evidence: Eligibility stores config, wallet, agency_index, role, and bump only
The admin certifies an unchecked wallet
There is no immutable X commitment, Premium tier, observation time, nonce, or verifier signature
impact: Non-Premium and unbound wallets can receive the higher Associate rate
The accepted per-pair cost model is bypassed
The chain cannot publicly audit why a wallet qualified
remediation: Verify an exact signed identity envelope on-chain
Bind wallet, immutable X commitment, active Premium tier, agency, role, freshness, nonce, and policy
Keep raw X IDs and OAuth tokens off-chain

findings.title: Agency registry padding can manipulate Associate pause economics
evidence: register_agency accepts an unchecked agency_owner without that owner's signature
Registration requires no Premium pair, stake, active position, bond, or expiry
Selection snapshots all registered agencies
impact: Permitted multi-wallet operators can cheaply add inactive agencies
Padding dilutes the probability that an economically active agency is selected and paused
Uniform random sampling can still produce economically manipulated outcomes
remediation: Require owner consent and a qualifying wallet/X/Premium attestation
Require an active bounded stake or bond and epoch eligibility
Publish padding and concentration simulations

findings.title: Associate settlement inherits the permanent CCC reveal-withholding deadlock
evidence: A permissionless payer initializes the unique round PDA
settle_position_week requires a settled CCC round for every non-standard role
There is no timeout, replacement, cancellation, or forced reveal path
impact: The first committer can permanently block an Associate week
Affected 52-week positions cannot fully settle or close
Reserved rewards remain locked
remediation: Implement bounded non-reroll recovery or forced resolution
Test the exact recovery path in host, SBF/local-validator, and signed Devnet flows
Obtain independent review of randomness liveness

findings.title: Associate certification is concentrated in the common administrator
evidence: register_agency and set_eligibility both require config.admin
The existing pre-launch audit records correlated upgrade, administration, and community-custody authority
impact: One authority can grant the higher-rate role and shape the candidate set
Compromise, coercion, or favoritism creates direct economic rents
remediation: Separate upgrade, eligibility, verifier, and custody roles
Use enforced threshold/timelock controls
Publish approvals and policy-bound eligibility receipts

findings.title: Eligibility can be overwritten without an explicit versioned lifecycle
evidence: The eligibility PDA uses init_if_needed
set_eligibility rewrites role and agency_index
No revision, expiry, revocation reason, or event is stored
impact: Current eligibility cannot be reconstructed from account state alone
Off-chain reviewers cannot distinguish correction, revocation, or discretionary reassignment
remediation: Define immutable/versioned eligibility receipts and events
Specify expiry, revocation, appeal, and effect on already-open positions

findings.title: The Associate DLC lacks its own economic cap and shutdown state
evidence: Associate rewards draw from common reward lanes
No Associate participant cap, obligation cap, activation budget, expiry, or terminal state exists
Individual positions reserve maximum obligations but aggregate Associate exposure is not separately published
impact: The future feature has no auditable standalone budget
Administrative enrollment can consume shared reward capacity and crowd out later positions
remediation: Publish exact aggregate Associate budget and enrollment behavior
Add fail-closed capacity and permanent terminal rules
Model concentration and lane-exhaustion outcomes

findings.title: Numeric role encoding is not self-describing at the account boundary
evidence: Role 2 is the Associate semantic
Eligibility and Position store only u8 role values
impact: Client or indexer drift can mislabel a financially meaningful role
remediation: Publish a versioned enum/interface digest and reject unknown versions
Include named role semantics in events and audit tooling
